Anagram.name: Anagram
Anagram.description: Letters of a word or phrase are rearranged to form the answer.
Anagram.indicator: Look out for words suggesting movement, change, or disorder: mix, throwing, destroy, strange, dancing, sort of, tampering with, exploded - these can all be anagram indicators.
Anagram.example: Clue: 'Traps laid for tin god' → Answer: 'SNARES' (letters of 'traps' rearranged)

Hidden Word.name: Hidden Word
Hidden Word.description: The answer appears consecutively inside words of the clue.
Hidden Word.indicator:
Look for words that suggest 
		 •Hiding or revealing: conceals, hides, displays, reveals.
		 •Containing: within, held by, capturing, absorbed. 
		 •A segment or part: sample, selection, bit of, taken from.
Hidden Word.example: Clue: 'Arab state within Romania' → Answer: 'OMAN' (hidden inside 'RoMANia')

Reversal.name: Reversal
Reversal.description: The answer appears backwards; indicated by words like 'back' or 'returns'.
Reversal.indicator:
Reversal indicators usually fall into three types: 
		 •Literal: back, returned, around, reversed, retro.
		 •Figurative: mirror, rolling, twist, circulating, boomerangs. 
		 •In down clues: words that suggest upwards motion - raising, up, lifted.
Reversal.example: Clue: 'Girl taking sodium backwards and forwards' → Answer: 'ANNA'

Homophone.name: Homophone
Homophone.description: The answer sounds like a word or phrase in the clue.
Homophone.indicator:
Homophone indicators usually relate to sound, speech, or hearing: sounded, listening to, mentioned, by phone, said, report, utterly, audition. 

 Some are clear, others more figurative, but they all suggest something you hear.
Homophone.example: Clue: 'An opening, so it's said, for love' → Answer: 'ADORE'

Double Definition.name: Double Definition
Double Definition.description: Two definitions in the clue point to the same answer.
Double Definition.indicator: The clue is often short and split into two distinct meanings that independently define the same answer. Punctuation (dash, question mark) or a smooth surface reading often separates the two definitions.

Container.name: Container
Container.description: Letters are placed inside other letters to form the answer.
Container.indicator:
There are two main types of container indicators:
		 •Within: in, into, within - insert letters into another word. 
		 •Around: about, around, outside of - wrap one word around another.
Container.example: Clue: 'Explicit about king in play' → Answer: 'CLEAR' ('C' around 'LEAR')

Subtraction.name: Subtraction
Subtraction.description: Some letters are removed to form the answer.
Subtraction.indicator: Look for words that suggest something being left out, removed, or ignored: without, drops, loses, gave up, forgotten by, cut, leaks out of.
Subtraction.example: Clue: 'Egyptian god beheading singers' → Answer: 'HORUS' ('chorus' minus the first letter)

Charade.name: Charade
Charade.description: Parts of the answer are clued separately and combined.
Charade.indicator:
There are three main types: 
		 •Singles: usually first, last, or middle letters. Look for words like head, tail, heart. If you're taking singles from multiple words, these indicators will be plural - e.g. heads. 
		 •Collections: outsides or insides of words. Think borders, coat, contents, guts. 
		 •Sequences: regularly spaced letters, like every second one. Indicators include odd, even, alternate, regularly.
Charade.example: Clue: 'Foxtrot by Romeo has to produce disapproving looks' → Answer: 'FROWNS'

Definition+Wordplay.name: Definition + Wordplay
Definition+Wordplay.description: One part is the straight definition and the other is wordplay.
Definition+Wordplay.indicator: There is usually no specific indicator for this structure itself. One part of the clue is a straight definition, while the other part contains wordplay indicators (anagram, container, deletion, etc.). The definition is almost always at the start or the end of the clue.
Definition+Wordplay.example: Clue: 'Just adjust my reel' → Answer: 'MERELY' (definition: just, wordplay: anagram of 'my reel')
